title: customer.subscription.deleted webhook writes 'cancelled' to both Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status
description: The handler's own code comment notes this dual-write 'fixes a real prior bug' where only one of the two status fields was updated, leaving the two records disagreeing about whether the org was cancelled. Regression guard to ensure a future refactor doesn't reintroduce the single-write bug. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no customer.subscription.deleted webhook, no Organization.subscription.status field usage, and no SubscriptionOrg model in the live code path (SubscriptionOrg is read-only in the one-time migration script only).
preconditions: Org has an active org-level Stripe subscription
steps: Trigger a customer.subscription.deleted event for the org's subscription
Read both Organization.subscription.status and the corresponding SubscriptionOrg.status after the webhook completes
expectedResult: Both fields read 'cancelled'. Neither is left stale/out of sync with the other.

title: Cancelling a pending downgrade with none scheduled stays a silent client no-op, not a surfaced error toast
description: billingService.cancelPendingChange() is called defensively in a few UI paths; the server's NO_PENDING_CHANGE code must keep being treated as success by the client so an org with nothing pending doesn't see a spurious error toast. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the server-side NO_PENDING_CHANGE response no longer exists (DELETE /v1/billing/plan/pending-change is gone); PendingDowngradeBanner.jsx still defensively checks for this dead error code client-side. See BILL-SAN-007.
steps: From the UI, trigger the cancel-pending-downgrade action (e.g. via PendingDowngradeBanner's Cancel, if rendered defensively even with nothing pending)
expectedResult: No error toast/banner appears; the call completes silently as a no-op, consistent with the server's NO_PENDING_CHANGE response.

title: Unhandled/unknown Stripe event types are acknowledged 200 rather than causing a 500 that triggers Stripe retry storms
description: Any event type without a registered handler (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded, which has no handler in this codebase) must still return 200 { received:true, ignored: event.type } so Stripe doesn't interpret it as a delivery failure and retry indefinitely. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no Stripe webhook endpoint or event types to acknowledge/ignore.
preconditions: A syntactically valid, correctly-signed Stripe event of a type with no registered handler (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded)
steps: Send this event to POST /webhooks/stripe with a valid signature
expectedResult: 200 { received:true, ignored:'payment_intent.succeeded' } and no stripe_events record is left in a 'failed' state; Stripe does not retry the delivery.

title: Immediate plan grandfathering must never zero an org's already-consumed ai.credits usage (2026-08-07 production incident)
description: Direct regression guard named in admin.controller.js's own code comment: a race between syncInstance()'s $setOnInsert carry and balance-row creation zeroed 3 orgs' visible ai.credits usage in production on 2026-08-07 despite real usage remaining intact underneath. The fix makes the carry an explicit unconditional $set.
preconditions: An org with non-zero usedValue/reservedValue on its current plan's EntitlementBalance rows
Admin performs a PATCH to that plan with grandfatheringMode='immediate'
steps: Concurrently trigger the plan update's grandfathering pass and a normal balance-row creation race (or otherwise force the internal $setOnInsert path to run before the controller's explicit carry)
Read the affected org's post-grandfathering EntitlementBalance rows
expectedResult: usedValue and reservedValue on every carried entitlement match their pre-grandfathering values exactly, regardless of internal timing — the explicit $set carry in _applyGrandfatheringImmediate() must win over any $setOnInsert race, never leaving a zeroed balance.

title: Stale AI-credit reservations older than ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION_TIMEOUT_MS are auto-cancelled by the term worker, except for sourceService b:storage and b:intelli-report
description: subscription-term.worker.js's tick() calls balance.service.expireStaleReservations(now - reservationTimeoutMs) every SUBSCRIPTION_TERM_INTERVAL_MS (default 60s), with a hard floor of 60s on the configured timeout. The two excluded sourceServices are deliberately long-lived reservations (storage holds, report generation) that must not be auto-cancelled by this sweep.
preconditions: A 'reserve' EntitlementUsageEvent with no commit/cancel, older than ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION_TIMEOUT_MS, sourceService='b:smart-compliance'
A second identically-stale reservation with sourceService='b:storage'
steps: Run (or wait for) the subscription-term worker's tick()
Check both reservations' finalization state afterward
expectedResult: The 'b:smart-compliance' reservation is auto-cancelled (a 'cancel' EntitlementUsageEvent is created and reservedValue is released). The 'b:storage' reservation is left untouched by this sweep, confirming the sourceService exclusion list is honored.

title: The term worker skips auto-renewing a SubscriptionInstance whose term has ended if a term-end change is already due for the same subject
description: subscription-term.worker.js's tick() checks for an approved/applying/failed SubscriptionRequest with desiredEffectiveAt<=now for the same subject before calling instances.renewCurrent() — preventing the worker from renewing the old plan in the same tick it should instead be replaced by an already-approved plan_change/downgrade/cancellation.
preconditions: An approved 'downgrade' SubscriptionRequest for the same subject with desiredEffectiveAt<=now, not yet applied
steps: Inspect whether renewCurrent() or apply() (or both) executed for this subject, and in what order
expectedResult: The due SubscriptionRequest is applied (via the dueRequests loop, which runs first in tick()) and the instance is not separately auto-renewed on its old plan in the same or a later tick for the same expired term — renewedInstances is not incremented for this subject once its pending change has applied.

title: Retired subscription models (SubscriptionOrg, SubscriptionProject, PendingTierChange) are never imported by live runtime code, and V2 behavior is not gated by rollout flags
description: Cross-referenced from an existing dev-authored Jest suite discovered during a repo-wide billing assessment: vibrantix-backend/tests/modules/subscription-v2-cutover.test.js already automates this exact guard (3 tests: no runtime file imports subscription-org.model/subscription-project.model/pending-tier-change.model; the retired model files themselves don't exist; no banned rollout-flag pattern gates V2 behavior). This QA-registry entry exists so the cutover's completeness has visibility in test-management-system too, not only in the dev test suite — the QA suite was previously unaware this automated coverage existed at all.
steps: Grep all live (non-test, non-migration) source files under vibrantix-backend/src for imports of subscription-org.model, subscription-project.model, or pending-tier-change.model
Confirm the three retired model files do not exist on disk
Grep for any rollout-flag pattern (e.g. a feature-flag check) gating V2 subscription behavior
expectedResult: Zero live imports of the three retired models, the model files themselves are absent, and no rollout flag conditionally enables/disables V2 behavior — the cutover is unconditional and complete, matching subscription-v2-cutover.test.js's own three assertions.
